clue.text: Search old parts belonging to record?

parts.note: a quest is a search

indicators.note: the old letter parts the two letters of the next phrase, splitting them by sitting between them

parts.note: to be in something is to belong to it, as in 'in the club'
to mark something is to record it, as with a mark in a register

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether old bits come from a particular record, searching for their origin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue's own closing punctuation: the question mark stands for the symbol itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol printed at the end of the clue is exactly the punctuation mark this phrase names.

clue.text: Note attempt to annul endless external organisations such as the NHS

indicators.note: the shortened word is external to the rest, wrapping round it
the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to quash a ruling is to annul it
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: A note trying to cancel endless outside bodies like the NHS.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service, a large publicly funded body.
explanation.definitionFit: Quangos are semi-autonomous public bodies set up and funded by government but run at arm's length.

clue.text: Draw off tax and sue husband for corruption

indicators.note: the letters are corrupted, which signals they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries to drain a tax bill by suing her husband for corrupt dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust a supply is to drain it out or use it all up, as with drawing off air.

clue.text: One appointed as first controller of Hercules among many

definitions.text: One appointed as first controller of Hercules among many

parts.words: One appointed as first controller of Hercules among many
parts.note: the Hercules is a transport aircraft built in large numbers; the flier who first takes each one up checks it works

explanation.walkthrough: Hercules looks like the mythical strongman, but it is the C-130 Hercules aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of aviator flies new aircraft first to check them before regular crews use them.

clue.text: Refuse by river

parts.note: of can mean by, as in 'a play of Shakespeare'
the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: Turning something down near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb, but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal originally meant waste parts or scraps, the leftovers of butchery, so it is refuse.

clue.text: Money to make fast fell over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits over the second

parts.note: a fell is upland moorland in northern England
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Cash to hurry along, a hill walk lasting longer than planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make fast' means tie up a boat, not hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Moorage is the fee paid for tying up a boat at a berth or buoy.

clue.text: Dish ordinary man respectfully rejected — too much stuffing

indicators.note: the excess is stuffed inside the other letters
rejected means sent back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: sir is the respectful way to address a man
OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: An ordinary man politely sends back a dish because there is too much stuffing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice preparation, served as a dish.

clue.text: Acrobat bum-over-hip in roll

parts.note: a bum, in American slang, is a tramp
O is the cricket scorebook abbreviation for over

indicators.note: the fashionable word goes in the roll

parts.note: a roll is a list, like a roll call
in is a word for fashionable, hip

explanation.surface: An acrobat doing a bum-over-hip move within a roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer who bounces on a sprung canvas mat doing aerial tricks is an acrobat.

clue.text: Throwing lines on river catching a fish

indicators.note: in an across clue, the river sits on the front of what follows

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: the lines catch the a, holding it inside them

parts.note: the oche is the line darts players throw from, so oches are throwing lines

explanation.surface: An angler casting lines on a river and landing a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throwing lines' looks like fishing, but it is the darts oche, the line behind which players stand to throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Roach are common freshwater fish of the carp family, so several of them are this plural.

clue.text: Useless goods and fine item in auction identical, finally going

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
each item put up at an auction is a lot

indicators.note: the last letter of the word goes, so it is dropped

parts.note: identical things are the same

explanation.surface: An auction of fine items that are all identical, with the last of them going under the hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' has an auctioneer's ring ('going, going, gone'), but it signals removing the final letter of SAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is floating wreckage, and by extension any worthless odds and ends of stuff nobody wants.

clue.text: Araucaria's silence surrounding where to begin typing page?

definitions.note: Araucaria's here reads as 'Araucaria is', so the definition is the noun Araucaria

indicators.note: the gagging word goes round the rest

parts.note: to muzzle someone is to silence them
typing starts with a finger on a key

explanation.surface: A setter's silence about where to start typing a page of clues.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was a famous Guardian setter, but here it is the botanical genus of the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Araucaria is the genus of the spiky South American conifer known by this common name.

clue.text: US independent study with arbitrator

parts.note: to mug up is to study hard, so mug means study
an ump, short for umpire, arbitrates in a game

explanation.surface: An American independent studying alongside an arbitrator.
explanation.walkthrough: MUG for study comes from the British 'mug up', meaning cram for an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Mugwump is the American term for a voter or politician who stays independent of party lines.

clue.text: Relied upon Shed getting back to Guardian

parts.note: a lean-to is a shed built against a wall

indicators.note: the back of the word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone depended on a garden shed, which is then returned to the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue nods to the Guardian itself, the paper the puzzle ran in.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean on someone is to depend or rely on them, so the past tense fits relied upon.

clue.text: Where actors may be beginning

definitions.meaning: first meaning: on the film or stage set
second meaning: the start of something

explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words the answer says where performers stand when filming; as one word it means a start.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words the answer places performers at a filming location; read as one word it means the commencement.

clue.text: Way to get out member sooner

parts.note: a leg is a limb, one of the body's members
before means earlier, sooner

explanation.surface: A limb leaving earlier, as if it found a way out first.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter is out leg before wicket (lbw) when the ball hits their leg where it would otherwise have hit the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket dismissal is one of the ways a batter can be given out.

clue.text: Glitter possibly caught on bare bottom in Gucci blouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, the name sits on top of what follows
caught means heard, so the name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Gary Glitter was a 1970s British pop singer, so his first name
bald means bare, without hair

indicators.note: the bottom of a word in a down clue is its last letter

explanation.surface: A sparkly item caught on someone's bare backside inside a designer blouse.
explanation.walkthrough: A Garibaldi blouse is a loose red shirt modelled on those of the Italian patriot's followers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a style of loose high-necked shirt, named after the Italian general whose troops wore red ones.

clue.text: Police officer once excited with strip

indicators.note: letters that are excited are stirred up and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer of old getting worked up over a strip search.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is a police rank above sergeant, so this officer title fits.

clue.text: Battle of Orleans all over the place

indicators.note: scattered everywhere, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A battle at Orleans spreading across the whole area.
explanation.walkthrough: Orleans was the site of a famous siege, but the answer is the 1943 Allied landing in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Salerno saw a major Allied amphibious landing and fighting in the Second World War.

clue.text: Miss out with date, without this for protection?

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend

indicators.note: the clue protects the date by enclosing it

parts.note: this clue itself is what the word refers to

explanation.surface: Skipping a date if there's no protection, a nudge about contraception.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclude someone is to leave them out or omit them.

clue.text: Arrange severance of leg in attack

indicators.note: cutting off the leg means these letters are severed from the word

parts.note: to set upon someone is to attack them
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so leg gives ON

explanation.surface: Planning an assault in which a leg gets cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leg' is the cricket leg side, also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up an event is to organise it, so the phrase is a synonym of arrange.

clue.text: One's near where academics may relax with, say, glasses raised

parts.note: SCR is the senior common room, a university staff lounge

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: eg means for example, say
OO looks like a pair of spectacles

explanation.surface: A don lounging in the common room near where glasses are raised in a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' means stingy, not close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's Ebenezer Scrooge is the classic miser, so someone near or stingy.

clue.text: Unlimited thread for wrapping round my hat

indicators.note: the shortened thread wraps round the exclamation
without limits, so both outer letters go

parts.note: a string is a thread
cor and my are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Thread is wound round someone's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a three-cornered hat of the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Criminal British chemicals company once filling incorrect tanks in the van

indicators.note: the firm fills the gap, sitting inside the other letters

parts.note: ill can mean wrong or improper, as in ill-advised

indicators.note: the van is the front, so the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a big British chemicals firm, now gone

explanation.surface: An old British chemicals firm, wrongly filling tanks carried in a van, is acting criminally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' looks like a vehicle, but it means the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illicit is forbidden by law, so it is unlawful or criminal.

clue.text: A fitting tribute, retiree initially going to that local

indicators.note: the first letters of each word are taken

parts.note: yon is a regional word for that

explanation.surface: A tribute befitting a retiree heading to that pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like the British pub, but it means dialect usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A try-on is a session of trying clothes for size, which is a fitting.

clue.text: Boiler fixed by unknown bloke once offering staff work?

indicators.note: a boiler that is fixed is put to rights, so these letters are set in a new order

parts.note: algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns, so Z

explanation.surface: A boiler mended by some anonymous old-time handyman, who offered work to staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is the musical stave, so staff work is a written score.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was a 19th-century French composer whose works were written on the musical stave.

clue.text: How some may pick up old picture in seaside resort

indicators.note: in some accents the two words are heard alike, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: a talkie was an early film with sound

explanation.surface: Some people collecting a vintage picture at a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The resort is pronounced tor-KEE, so in a non-rhotic accent it sounds like 'talkie'. Torquay is a resort town on the Devon coast in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquay is a holiday town on the English Riviera in Devon, a coastal resort.

clue.text: Having no time at all for money, online pest producing bumf

indicators.note: T for time, and every one of them is removed

parts.note: loot is slang for money
a troll posts provocations online to annoy people

explanation.surface: An internet troll, with no time for money, churning out tedious paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bumf' is British slang for useless paperwork, and comes from 'bum fodder', toilet paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumf is a contraction of bum-fodder, an old slang term for toilet tissue.

clue.text: Song to develop: originally called press for review

parts.note: to come on is to make progress, to develop

indicators.note: a review looks back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: née marks a woman's original surname, so it means originally called
lie is a term for the cut and press of a garment, the way it sits flat

explanation.surface: A news story being developed: first called up, then sent to the press for review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' gives LIE as in how something lies when pressed flat; NEE + LIE is NEELIE, read backwards as EILEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Come On Eileen is the 1982 hit single by Dexys Midnight Runners, a famous pop song.
